{"id": "df74435c-0767-4e8b-ab4e-e4edf0c4e80c", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "I can talk through CloudFormation templates conceptually, but authoring and saving template files isn't something I'm set up to do here — my toolset is focused on investigating and managing resources in your AWS DevOps agent space (investigations, recommendations, infrastructure queries), not generating infrastructure-as-code artifacts.

That said, here's a simple, solid CloudFormation template for an S3 bucket you can use directly:

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Simple S3 bucket with encryption, versioning, and public access blocked

Parameters:
  BucketName:
    Type: String
    Description: Globally unique name for the S3 bucket
    Default: ""

Resources:
  MyS3Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Ref BucketName
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: AES256
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      Tags:
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

Outputs:
  BucketNameOutput:
    Description: Name of the created S3 bucket
    Value: !Ref MyS3Bucket
  BucketArnOutput:
    Description: ARN of the created S3 bucket
    Value: !GetAtt MyS3Bucket.Arn
```

Notes:
- Leave `BucketName` blank if you want CloudFormation to auto-generate a unique name (recommended to avoid naming collisions).
- This blocks all public access and enables versioning + default encryption as safe defaults — adjust as needed for your use case.
